title: Chapter 123 — The Leader's Scorecard and Operating Rituals
intro: The leadership dashboard, team rituals, and the leader's own feedback loop.

sections.title: What Leaders Should Measure
sections.content:
The leader's scorecard is different from the salesperson's scorecard. Leaders measure team closing percentage, team average ticket, pipeline health across the team, training completion, coaching hours logged, employee retention, customer satisfaction, and store profitability.

These tell you whether you are building a healthy business — not just hitting a sales number.

sections.title: The Leader's Rituals
sections.content:
Daily: walk the floor, observe interactions, coach one person. Weekly: team huddle, individual check-ins, pipeline review. Monthly: financial review, training assessment. Quarterly: strategic planning, goal setting.

Rituals create consistency. Consistency creates culture. Culture creates results.

sections.title: The Feedback Loop
sections.content:
Leaders need feedback too. From their team, from their manager, from their customers, from their numbers.

The leader who thinks they have nothing to improve is the one who has the most to improve. Stay curious. Stay humble. Ask your team: what could I be doing better?

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating leadership operating systems, ask:

Is the leader measuring the right things — or just the easy things?
Do they maintain consistent rituals — or lead reactively?
Are they open to feedback — or closed to it?
Is the team getting stronger under their leadership — or staying the same?
